profiles.meeting_scenario: A coordination meeting at a university law school between two faculty members preparing a jointly authored public-law memo for an internal symposium on governance and decentralization in China, with the possibility that parts of the memo may later be repurposed into an amicus-related background document. The memo will draw on a paper about China's regionally decentralized authoritarian system and must be coordinated across two workstreams: one member will shape the doctrinal and court-facing framing, while the other will assemble the underlying sources, translations, and comparative institutional support. The agenda is to align on what should go into the shared source bundle for next Thursday's faculty circulation, which version of the paper should anchor the analysis, what it means for citations to be ready in the draft, and how responsibility for maintaining the shared materials will pass between them during the week. The expected outcome is an apparently smooth handoff in which both leave believing they know what materials will be available, what degree of citation completion the draft will have, and how the shared repository will be kept current.

members.name: Elena Park
members.role: Clinical Professor and Supervising Attorney, Public Law Appellate Clinic
members.expertise: Appellate briefing, administrative law, amicus coordination, court-ready source management
members.background: Elena spent eight years in a state solicitor general's office before joining the law school clinic, where she now supervises student teams producing appellate briefs and public-law filings that often begin as faculty-facing memoranda before becoming litigation materials.
members.private_state: She wants the collaboration to produce a clean, reusable set of materials that can move quickly into clinic workflow if an external opportunity arises, and she is especially concerned about avoiding a late-stage scramble caused by unstable citations or shifting source files.
hidden_assumptions: When someone says the supporting materials for a faculty draft, they usually mean the relatively clean set of sources a downstream legal writer can safely cite from without sorting through research debris.
The current paper is the published version already circulating among faculty because that is the version most likely to serve as the stable citation anchor in any later external-facing document.
If citations are in place for circulation, each quoted or paraphrased proposition already has verified pincites and usable source information, even if stylistic polishing remains.
If Victor is handling the shared materials until she starts drafting, he will maintain them as a controlled handoff set that becomes effectively fixed once she begins pulling from it.

members.name: Victor Chen
members.expertise: Chinese legal institutions, law-and-development scholarship, bilingual source synthesis
members.background: Victor is a comparative law scholar with a JD/PhD background who works extensively with Chinese-language policy texts, conference drafts, and evolving article versions, and he often supports interdisciplinary projects by curating broader research context rather than only court-citable authorities.
members.private_state: He wants to preserve analytical nuance from the scholarship and keep the record broad enough to withstand faculty questions about regional variation, source lineage, and the difference between formal legal rules and local implementation.
hidden_assumptions: Supporting materials for a faculty memo naturally include not just polished authorities but also contextual research items, translation notes, and earlier drafts that help explain the argument's institutional logic.
The current paper is the most analytically complete version in active scholarly use, even if that version is a later SSRN revision rather than the published print article.

If citations are in place for circulation, the draft has identified the right authorities and general locations, while exact pincites, translation parentheticals, and formatting can still be refined after comments.
If he is carrying the shared materials during the week, he can continue enriching and reorganizing them as understanding develops until Elena actually needs to freeze portions for prose drafting.

misalignment_points.topic: What belongs in the supporting materials
misalignment_points.surface_form: They agree that Victor will assemble 'the supporting materials' for next Thursday's draft.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 takes this to mean a relatively clean source bundle consisting of the paper itself, citable translations where available, and a limited set of directly usable background authorities that can feed straight into legal drafting.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 takes this to mean a broader research bundle that includes the main paper plus contextual items such as working-paper versions, informal translation notes, policy excerpts, and comparative materials that illuminate the argument.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: The phrase 'supporting materials' is generic and cooperative-sounding, so it creates false consensus without inviting itemization; each hears a normal category from their own workflow and sees no need to enumerate contents in a short coordination call.

misalignment_points.topic: Which document is the current paper
misalignment_points.surface_form: They refer to 'the current paper' and 'the version people have been using.'
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 is thinking of the published journal article already circulated to faculty and likely to anchor any formal citations.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 is thinking of the later SSRN or post-conference revision with expanded notes and wording he regards as the operative scholarly version.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: Both documents share the same author, thesis, and much of the same text, so ordinary references to 'the paper' feel fully adequate; the differences matter in footnotes, framing, and source architecture rather than in the headline proposition.

misalignment_points.topic: What it means for citations to be ready
misalignment_points.surface_form: They agree the draft should have 'citations in place' before faculty circulation.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 believes this means propositions in the circulated draft already have verified pincites, stable source metadata, and citation locations solid enough that later clinic work will not require basic reconstruction.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 believes this means the correct authorities and approximate supporting passages have been identified in the draft, even if exact pincites, translation qualifiers, and Bluebook details are still to be cleaned up later.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: The phrase 'citations in place' sounds routine and intermediate rather than absolute, so both can honestly agree while applying different completion thresholds; in academic-legal collaborations the phrase often functions as a vague readiness signal rather than a precise standard.

misalignment_points.topic: What it means for Victor to carry the shared materials this week
misalignment_points.surface_form: They agree that Victor will 'carry the shared materials' until Elena starts drafting from them.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 assumes this means Victor is the temporary custodian of a handoff set that he will keep current but effectively stabilize for her use once she begins drafting, so she can treat the repository as a dependable source base.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 assumes this means he remains the active owner of the research repository during the week and may continue adding, replacing, and re-sorting materials even as Elena starts drawing from it, unless she specifically asks him to freeze it.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: The phrase 'carry the shared materials' sounds like a mundane responsibility assignment about ownership rather than method; both think they have aligned on who is in charge, while silently importing different norms about when a research repository becomes a fixed handoff package.
